title: pvComputeQuartiles
body:
## pvComputeQuartiles

Computes, for every single-component numeric array, the five order statistics minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum, and outputs them as a table (vtkTable) with one column per array and five rows. For a dataset the point-data arrays are used; a table input uses its columns, and composite input adds one column per block (suffix _Block_<id>). Use it for box-plot style summaries of a field's distribution; use pvHistogram for the full distribution.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Multi-component arrays such as velocity are skipped, not reduced to magnitude; compute a magnitude array first if you need its quartiles.
- Cell-data arrays of a dataset are not summarised; convert them with cellToPoint or extract them to a table first.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `ComputeQuartiles`. Identity: `filters/ComputeQuartiles`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the filter. Accepted data: any data object (vtkDataObject). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataObject"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Syntax example

```json

  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvComputeQuartiles",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
